maya: FYI getting alerts: multiple gen-serving pods Pending in gpu-nodepool-us-west1 :warning:
maya: CA logs look like it's refusing to scale due to surge budget? not 100% sure

li: can you paste the CA log lines around the time pods started queuing?

maya: pasted below:
```
I0304 14:12:03.123456       1 core.go:272] checking unregistered pods
I0304 14:12:03.123789       1 static_autoscaler.go:236] No node group increase: max nodes reached for nodegroup gpu-pool-usw1
I0304 14:12:03.123999       1 scale_up.go:441] Scale-up failed: would exceed max surge nodes (current 8, max 8)
I0304 14:12:03.124200       1 event.go:218] Normal ScaleUp: No unschedulable pods (filtered by taints/tolerations)
```

maya: note the "max nodes reached" + "would exceed max surge nodes" lines

li: ah, we set a strict maxSize on that nodepool after last cost optimization (max 8 GPUs). HPA triggered replica increases, CA wants new nodes but hits max. HPA then keeps increasing pods -> Pending backlog.

tariq: wait — why is CA complaining about surge? that's more about rollout surge, not autoscaler. In GKE there's a node pool autoscaling max. Are we mixing with cluster upgrade surge settings?

sana: There are two separate controls: nodepool autoscaler maxSize, and the cluster autoscaler also has a concept of scale-up limits if there's an in-flight resize. But the error is consistent with maxSize hit. Also saw PodDisruptionBudget stalling some evictions earlier which made pod redistribution brittle.

maya: HPA was scaling from 6 -> 12 because custom metric qps_per_replica spiked. QPS metric source is our prometheus-adapter. I suspect metric delay made HPA overshoot while CA couldn't keep up.

li: copy of HPA config we used (redacted):
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gen-serving-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    kind: Deployment
    name: gen-serving
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: custom/qps_per_replica
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "75"
```

li: HPA maxReplicas 20 vs nodepool maxSize 8 -> mismatch. CA can't create enough GPU nodes.

tariq: two questions: 1) why did HPA keep scaling after CA failed? 2) what's lowest-impact mitigation?

sana: answers: 1) HPA does not know capacity limits of nodes; it only reacts to metrics. If pods are Pending, HPA still tries to hit target replicas unless there's an external signal. 2) mitigations: lower HPA maxReplicas, or create a separate burst nodepool with higher maxSize/cheaper preemptible GPUs and allow CA to scale it, or add a custom admission webhook that prevents new replicas when scheduling pressure is high.

maya: ops-bot alerted devs saying nodes are "Reached max nodes" and started rolling back canaries; we already had a canary deployment concurrently so rollout + HPA = bad combo.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: nodegroup gpu-pool-usw1 at max size (8). Pending pods: 14. Pending due to insufficient resources: nvidia.com/gpu=1.

li: I propose temporary quickfix: reduce HPA.maxReplicas to 8 and scale down HPA targets to match node capacity, then open a ticket to add a burst GPU nodepool.

tariq: +1. Also add a saturation metric alert for prometheus: when PendingPods > 5 for more than 2m, mute HPA (or throttle) — we can implement a simple controller that annotation-blocks ReplicaSet scaling via a small webhook.

sana: alternative: allow CA to scale up another node pool (cheaper preemptible) by labeling pods with nodeSelector for burst-pool. But that requires updating Deployment rollout; might be fine for emergency.

maya: I've temporarily set HPA.maxReplicas=8 and scaled gen-serving deployment replicas=8 manually. Observing CA now: it freed some Pending pods onto existing nodes by evicting low-priority pods.

tariq: long term action items:
- add capacity-aware HPA docs + runbook (sana)
- create burst-gpu nodepool config with maxSize 30, taint gpu-burst=true:NoSchedule, tolerations in deploys for burst-enabled (li)
- add Prometheus alert for Pending pods and CA max-size hit (maya)
- evaluate introducing a pre-scale controller that queries CA capacity before HPA applies scale events (tariq)

maya: thanks everyone. Reopening if it resurfaces. :thumbsup:

autoscaler-bot: [info] cluster-autoscaler: scale-up events after HPA change: started 2 new nodes in gpu-pool-usw1-burst

li: recording the thread into incident doc. will include exact timestamps & metrics.

sana: also note VPA was in "recommend" mode for some non-gpu sidecars earlier; we should ensure VPA doesn't evict pods during scale events.

maya: closing for now, we'll follow the action list.
